explain.es: Go the extra mile = esforzarse más de lo requerido; elbow grease = esfuerzo físico; put your shoulder to the wheel = trabajar con empeño; pull your socks up, británico, = mejorar el esfuerzo o conducta. Literalmente: milla, codo, hombro y calcetines.
explain.en: These expressions concern extra effort, hard physical work, energetic participation, and improving one's performance. Literal milla, codo, hombro, and calcetines miss those instructions. Pull your socks up is British.

title.es: -ÓN ya no se traduce simplemente como BIG
title.en: -ÓN no longer translates simply as BIG

explain.es: Estas formas relacionadas con caja, camisa, cintura y tapa tienen nombres propios en inglés: drawer, nightdress, belt y stopper. El sufijo aumentativo quedó lexicalizado; big box, shirt, waist o lid no daría estas traducciones.
explain.en: These words developed from forms related to box, shirt, waist, and lid, but now translate as drawer, nightdress, belt, and stopper. Their lexicalized meanings cannot be recovered simply by adding big.

title.es: Una vocal final cambia la pista
title.en: A final vowel changes the clue

explain.es: Balde = bucket, ganga = bargain, firma = signature y tropa = troops. Bald significa calvo; gang, pandilla; firm, empresa o firme; trope, recurso figurativo o motivo recurrente.
explain.en: These Spanish nouns mean bucket, bargain, signature, and troops. Their lookalikes bald, gang, firm, and trope point to hairlessness, a group, a business or firmness, and a figurative device.

title.es: El cuerpo expresa actitudes y situaciones
title.en: The body expresses attitudes and situations

explain.es: Dar el brazo a torcer = yield; a lo hecho, pecho = face the consequences; dar la espalda = reject or abandon; estar hasta el cuello = be deeply involved or overwhelmed. Literalmente son arm, chest, back y neck.
explain.en: These expressions concern yielding, facing consequences, rejecting someone, and being deeply involved or overwhelmed. The literal body parts are arm, chest, back, and neck.

title.es: Deportes con nombres tomados del inglés
title.en: Sports with names borrowed from English

explain.es: Corresponden a boxing, cricket, badminton y baseball. El español adaptó estos nombres ingleses; aquí las diferencias ortográficas no representan diferencias de significado.
explain.en: These correspond to boxing, cricket, badminton, and baseball. Spanish adapted the English names while retaining the sports' meanings.

title.es: TENER un sustantivo, BE un adjetivo
title.en: TENER a noun, BE an adjective

explain.es: Tener sed = be thirsty; tener hambre = be hungry; tener sueño = be sleepy; tener miedo = be afraid. En estas traducciones naturales, el inglés cambia tener más sustantivo por be más adjetivo.
explain.en: Spanish uses TENER with these nouns where English naturally uses BE with adjectives: thirsty, hungry, sleepy, and afraid.

title.es: El inglés entra a la oficina

explain.es: Printear y taipear adaptan print y type en español estadounidense; fólder adapta folder y es común en México y otros países americanos. Escanear, de scan, ya pertenece al español general. Son préstamos con distintos grados de integración.
explain.en: US Spanish printear and taipear adapt print and type. Fólder adapts folder in Mexico and elsewhere in the Americas. Escanear, from scan, is established in general Spanish. The borrowings differ in how widely integrated they are.

title.en: English images of annoyance and anger

explain.es: Drive someone up the wall = desesperar; hit the roof = enfurecerse; the last straw = la gota que colma el vaso; get someone's goat = irritar. Literalmente: pared, techo, paja y cabra.
explain.en: These expressions concern intense annoyance, anger, a final intolerable incident, and irritation. Literal Spanish pared, techo, paja, and cabra do not explain those reactions.

explain.es: Mercado → market → supermarket; héroe → hero → superhero; potencia → power → superpower; natural → natural → supernatural.
explain.en: Translate to market, hero, power, and natural, then prepend SUPER: supermarket, superhero, superpower, and supernatural.

title.es: El diminutivo ya tiene traducción propia
title.en: The diminutive has its own translation

explain.es: En estos sentidos, ventanilla = ticket window; bolsillo = pocket; mesilla = bedside table; casilla = box de un formulario. Traducir únicamente como little window, bag, table o house perdería el nombre convencional.
explain.en: These lexicalized diminutives have conventional translations: ticket window, pocket, bedside table, and a form's box. Simply adding little to the underlying Spanish noun's translation misses the intended object.

title.es: Parecidos engañosos entre papeles y registros
title.en: Misleading lookalikes among papers and records

explain.es: Dato = fact o piece of information, frente a date, fecha; reclamo puede ser complaint, frente a reclaim, recuperar; estampa puede ser print, frente a stamp, sello; suplente = substitute, frente a supplement, complemento.
explain.en: The intended Spanish readings are a fact, a complaint, a printed image, and a substitute. Date, reclaim, stamp, and supplement suggest different meanings. Some words have additional senses beyond these contrasts.

title.es: Lecturas españolas detrás de palabras inglesas

explain.es: En español: salve puede ser una salutación; bares, establecimientos; lees, tú read; pinto, I paint. En inglés: salve = ungüento; bares = deja al descubierto; lees = sedimentos; pinto = caballo de manchas.
explain.en: Spanish offers a greeting, drinking establishments, you read, and I paint. English instead supplies an ointment, exposes, sediment, and a spotted horse.

explain.es: Stick your neck out = arriesgarse por alguien o algo; go out on a limb = adoptar una posición arriesgada; be on thin ice = estar en situación precaria; take the plunge = decidirse a actuar. Literalmente: cuello, rama o extremidad, hielo y zambullida.
explain.en: These expressions concern taking a personal risk, adopting an exposed position, being in a precarious situation, and finally committing to action. Literal neck, limb, ice, and plunge do not capture the decisions involved.

explain.es: Estima → esteem → self-esteem; servicio → service → self-service; retrato → portrait → self-portrait; defensa → defense → self-defense.
explain.en: Translate to esteem, service, portrait, and defense, then prepend SELF: self-esteem, self-service, self-portrait, and self-defense.

title.es: Sustantivos cotidianos que cambian la escena
title.en: Everyday nouns that change the scene

explain.es: Boda = wedding, no body; dinero = money, no dinner; trampa = trap, no tramp; vaso = drinking glass, no vase. Body es cuerpo; dinner, cena; tramp puede ser caminante; vase, florero.
explain.en: These Spanish words mean wedding, money, trap, and drinking glass. Their lookalikes body, dinner, tramp, and vase instead suggest a body, a meal, a walker, and a flower container.

explain.es: Marqueta viene de market, documentada en el noreste estadounidense; londri, de laundry; grocería, de grocery, ambas estadounidenses; guachimán, de watchman, documentado en México y otros países americanos. Nombran mercado, lavandería, tienda de comestibles y vigilante.
explain.en: These borrow market, laundry, grocery, and watchman. Marqueta is documented in the northeastern US; londri and grocería in US Spanish; guachimán in Mexico and other American countries. They name neighborhood businesses and a guard.

title.en: English ways to say something costs a fortune

explain.es: Cost an arm and a leg, pay through the nose, cost the earth y cost a king's ransom expresan un precio enorme. Literalmente evocan brazo, nariz, tierra y rescate. Cost the earth está especialmente asociado al inglés británico.
explain.en: These expressions describe paying an enormous amount. Literal Spanish brazo, nariz, tierra, and rescate preserve the images but miss the price judgment. Cost the earth is especially associated with British English.

title.es: TRUNK cambia de equipaje a naturaleza
title.en: TRUNK moves from luggage to nature

explain.es: Trunk puede ser baúl, trompa de elefante, tronco de árbol o maletero de automóvil. El último sentido corresponde al inglés estadounidense.
explain.en: TRUNK can mean a storage chest, an elephant's appendage, a tree's main stem, or a car's luggage compartment. The automobile sense is US English.
